Content:
26:08 My partner and i have 2 experiences of hearing us calling each other, even tho it wasnt us who did it.


The first instance was in his old house, we would hang out in his basement a lot [it had a couch, fairy lights a tv, the works.] It was me, our 2 ex friends and him, we were chilling and my partner goes upstairs to get some snacks and stuff; for context the basement door is on carpet and its hinges are very squeaky and loud, so you can 100% hear someone opening and closing the door. Now about 2 minutes pass and all of us hear the basement door open and  my partner call for me to go upstairs, i think nothing of it cuz he's probably just asking for help bringing stuff down the stairs, but when i got halfway towards the stairs, the basement door opened again and here comes my partner with snacks and drinks. We all asked him "did you call for them [me]?" And he said "no i was in the other room looking for snacks". We all just looked at each other freaked out. 
We moved out of the house a few months later.

The second experience is in our current house. My partner and I were chilling in the living room, watching tv. I leaves the room to go to the bathroom [we have 2 bathrooms a full and a half]. when i came back out my partner was staring at the upstairs, he whipped his head around as i round the corner and he frantically asks "did you call for me?" i said "no". An we just stared at each other freaked out, trying to joke about it like "there's no way IT followed us here" ToT

We till have some instances where we hear each other call for one another, only to realize it wasnt us.

Content: Shawn the loud sound you described in real life sounds like a window blow out, i had it happen to me when we had new windows put in, and if it is you might find fogging / moister build up over time between the 2 panels of the double glazing... A window blow out refers to two different issues: a blown double-glazed unit that is foggy between the panes, or a window that has failed structurally and broken or been forcefully removed. A blown double-glazed unit occurs when the seal fails, allowing moisture in, which can make the window look cloudy, reduce its efficiency, and cause drafts. A structurally failed window is a more serious issue, potentially caused by wind, damage, or poor installation, and requires immediate repair, such as boarding up the opening and replacing the window

I was terrified. I live alone with my son, and I'm a very thin woman. Scary, ok? Anyways, next morning i go downstairs and see that the shelf above my washer & dryer was all fcked up. I have some boxes and flower pots and random stuff up there. The shelf is part of the wall, so it didn't "come loose" but the stuff that was on that shelf, was now on the floor the next morning. How tf did that happen? Doors were locked. Son was dead asleep. He sleeps like a rock so he didn't even wake up to the noise. I still have no idea what happened but it was weird af.
Dude... my son is almost 13 and in middle school. First of all, WHAT?? Already?! NO! 
Second, i still vividly remember being 12 and 13. It feels like that was just a few years ago! I can't believe how fast time goes by. 
And third, it's crazy to think that people our age (early to mid 30s) are the last gen to know what it was like before all this modern tech. We saw the invention of the smart phones, tablets, touch screens, the modern internet, Google, MySpace, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube... I didn't have internet at home until i was 12 or 13. Same with most of my friends.  As a young kid, we had basic cable with about 30 something channels. Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, VH1, Comedy Central, AMC, ABC, PBS, TNT... 
I wonder what kind of effect this newer technological age will have on our kids/the younger gens? And can you imagine what life will be like in 20 years? 50? 100? With VR and AR and neurological implants and AI.... kinda scary to think about.

Edit: so, in case someone is wondering the story that Jack almost missed. The Blackwood family consisted of the husband, Eleanor (the wife), Agnes (the maid), and Emily (the little girl), and some other servants/maids. They hired Agnus to help during the house renovations, to make sure Emily didn't get hurt. Well, everyone started liking and loving Agnus, which made Eleanor jealous. One of the evidence you can din that the husband DID have feelings for Agnus, but felt guilty about it (so he's not THAT bad of a guy). Eventually, a fire broke out, and Eleanor took the chance to blame Agnus (who seemed to have a hatred for Eleanor because...women, am I right?) Emily died in that fire, and Agnus tried saving her, but still go blamed. The husband decided to believe Eleanor finally, and told Eleanor to kill Agnus, which she did by hanging her (hence the rope you find and the shadow of the hanging lady). They buried her in the basement while they were pouring concrete, but obviously, Agnus isn't happy. Shit went down. Eleanor when batshit crazy and killed herself, the kids (I guess they had more kids eventually?) left because the father started drinking, and he died a sour old man. And because of the fire and the children not wanting anything to do with the family, everyone forgot about it. Making Agnus EVEN MORE PISSED. So when kids go poking around in places they shouldn't (typical horror movie characters), they get fucked up. The only question is, how did a literal ghost butcher, maime, and string up dead college kids like meat?
